answer: Latency Debt Registration. Each new identity must solve a fresh cipher tied to its origin address, and the solved key is held escrowed by a randomly assigned nebula relay for 90 days before the identity can transact. Attacker cost is wall-clock time plus escrow lockup per identity: creating N sybils serializes key release across N distinct relays, so a farm of 10,000 identities pays 10,000 parallel escrow slots and sustained relay bandwidth. A single island of honest identities shares one relay pool, keeping their per-identity cost near zero while duplication scales linearly.
